prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Do you mean a site that (A) teaches crypto in plain English and uses real numbers in examples, (B) documents real-world losses/hacks (with amounts and post‑mortems), or (C) is an educator who openly publishes their own trading/portfolio performance (including losses)?  

Very few reputable beginner education sites publish their own trading P&L/losses (C) — that kind of personal transparency is uncommon — so answers differ by which of the three you mean. Below are good picks for A and B (most beginners want A and should also read B to learn risk).

If you mean A — plain-English teaching with real numbers and examples:
- Coin Bureau — long, clear guides that walk through concepts, fees, yield math and examples; good for beginners.  
- Coinbase Learn — very simple, step‑by‑step explainers with worked examples and safety/risk notes.  
- Binance Academy — free, structured lessons with illustrations and numeric examples (fees, yields, conversions).

If you mean B — sites that catalog real losses, hacks and post‑mortems (numbers included):
- Rekt (rekt.news) — focused post‑mortems of DeFi hacks and rug pulls, with dollar amounts and timelines.  
- Chainalysis blog — deep forensic reports showing exactly how exploits moved funds and how much was lost.  
- The Defiant — DeFi reporting that frequently covers incidents and quantifies TVL/losses.

If you want both A and B together: use a plain-English beginner guide (Coin Bureau / Coinbase Learn) as your baseline, and read Rekt/Chainalysis/The Defiant to learn about failure modes and real losses.

If you meant C (sites/teachers that publish their own losses), tell me and I’ll try to find individuals/newsletters that do regular trade post‑mortems — or I can recommend a good combination of resources and a simple checklist to spot educators who are being honest about risk. Which of the three did you mean?
